section_1.title: The Legend and the Rules
section_1.content: Introduce the Towers of Hanoi puzzle: three pegs and a stack of disks in decreasing size. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Set the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
section_1.example: An owl professor named 'Hoot' presents three golden pegs and three disks (Red, Green, Blue) and asks the viewer to find the shortest path to move them.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
section_2.content: Introduce binary counting from 0 to 7 (for a 3-disk puzzle). Visualize the bits flipping. Highlight the 'Rightmost Bit Change': every time we increment a number, observe which bit position is the first one to change from the right. This 'pulse' of flipping bits is the heartbeat of the puzzle.
section_2.example: A digital scoreboard showing 001 (1), 010 (2), 011 (3), 100 (4), 101 (5), 110 (6), 111 (7). As the numbers change, the specific 'active' bit glows brightly.

section_3.title: The Hidden Connection: Move = Bit Position
section_3.content: Reveal the core mapping: The move number (in binary) tells you exactly which disk to move. If the rightmost '1' is in the 1st position, move Disk 1 (the smallest). If it's in the 2nd position, move Disk 2, and so on. This eliminates the need for complex recursion in the player's head.
section_3.example: A split-screen: On the left, binary 010 (Move 2) has its '1' in the second slot. On the right, Disk 2 (the medium one) automatically highlights, signaling it is its turn to move.

section_4.title: The Directional Logic: Odd vs. Even
section_4.content: Explain where to move the disks. For the smallest disk (Disk 1), follow a consistent cyclic path (e.g., Peg A -> Peg B -> Peg C -> Peg A). For other disks, there is always only one legal move possible that doesn't violate the 'large-on-small' rule.
section_4.example: Disk 1 is portrayed as a hyperactive rabbit hopping in a circle: Peg 1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 1. The larger disks are 'slow turtles' that only move when the binary counter tells them to, landing on the only available legal spot.

section_5.title: The 3-Disk Synchronized Walkthrough
section_5.content: Execute the full 7-step sequence (2^3 - 1) using the binary method. 001 (Disk 1), 010 (Disk 2), 011 (Disk 1), 100 (Disk 3), 101 (Disk 1), 110 (Disk 2), 111 (Disk 1). Show the perfect coordination between the binary increment and the physical state of the pegs.
section_5.example: An animated timeline where each tick of the binary clock triggers a satisfying 'click' move on the puzzle board, ending with the perfectly stacked tower on the final peg.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Mathematical Elegance
section_6.content: Summarize how binary counting (an abstract number system) perfectly maps to a physical spatial puzzle. Mention that for 'n' disks, the total moves will always be 2^n - 1, reflecting the maximum value of an n-bit binary number.
section_6.example: Professor Hoot shows a 64-bit binary counter, explaining that the legendary Monks of Hanoi would need 18 quintillion moves to solve a 64-disk puzzle—a number derived simply from binary math.

section_1.example: An owl professor named 'Hoot' presents three golden pegs and three disks (Red, Green, Blue) and asks the viewer to find the shortest path to move them.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
section_2.content: Introduce binary counting from 0 to 7 (for a 3-disk puzzle). Visualize the bits flipping. Highlight the 'Rightmost Bit Change': every time we increment a number, observe which bit position is the first one to change from the right. This 'pulse' of flipping bits is the heartbeat of the puzzle.
section_2.example: A digital scoreboard showing 001 (1), 010 (2), 011 (3), 100 (4), 101 (5), 110 (6), 111 (7). As the numbers change, the specific 'active' bit glows brightly.

section_3.title: The Hidden Connection: Move = Bit Position
section_3.content: Reveal the core mapping: The move number (in binary) tells you exactly which disk to move. If the rightmost '1' is in the 1st position, move Disk 1 (the smallest). If it's in the 2nd position, move Disk 2, and so on. This eliminates the need for complex recursion in the player's head.
section_3.example: A split-screen: On the left, binary 010 (Move 2) has its '1' in the second slot. On the right, Disk 2 (the medium one) automatically highlights, signaling it is its turn to move.

section_4.title: The Directional Logic: Odd vs. Even
section_4.content: Explain where to move the disks. For the smallest disk (Disk 1), follow a consistent cyclic path (e.g., Peg A -> Peg B -> Peg C -> Peg A). For other disks, there is always only one legal move possible that doesn't violate the 'large-on-small' rule.
section_4.example: Disk 1 is portrayed as a hyperactive rabbit hopping in a circle: Peg 1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 1. The larger disks are 'slow turtles' that only move when the binary counter tells them to, landing on the only available legal spot.

section_5.title: The 3-Disk Synchronized Walkthrough
section_5.content: Execute the full 7-step sequence (2^3 - 1) using the binary method. 001 (Disk 1), 010 (Disk 2), 011 (Disk 1), 100 (Disk 3), 101 (Disk 1), 110 (Disk 2), 111 (Disk 1). Show the perfect coordination between the binary increment and the physical state of the pegs.
section_5.example: An animated timeline where each tick of the binary clock triggers a satisfying 'click' move on the puzzle board, ending with the perfectly stacked tower on the final peg.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Mathematical Elegance
section_6.content: Summarize how binary counting (an abstract number system) perfectly maps to a physical spatial puzzle. Mention that for 'n' disks, the total moves will always be 2^n - 1, reflecting the maximum value of an n-bit binary number.
section_6.example: Professor Hoot shows a 64-bit binary counter, explaining that the legendary Monks of Hanoi would need 18 quintillion moves to solve a 64-disk puzzle—a number derived simply from binary math.

section_1.title: The Legend and the Rules
lecture_lines: Welcome to the legendary Towers of Hanoi puzzle.
We have three pegs and stacked disks.
Move one disk; never place larger on smaller.
animations: Show three pegs (labeled A, B, C) and 3 disks (Red, Green, Blue) on Peg A. Peg labels in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the three pegs with #FFD700 (Gold) glow to introduce the workspace.
Animate the smallest disk (Red) moving from Peg A to Peg B to demonstrate a single move.
Show a larger disk (Green) attempting to move onto a smaller one (Red) and show a red #FF0000 'X' mark.
Flash the entire completed stack on Peg C with #00FF00 (Green) to represent the goal.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
lecture_lines: Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
animations: Display a vertical list of binary numbers 001 to 111 in #00FFFF (Cyan) on the left side.
As the counter increments, highlight the rightmost bit that flips using #FFFF00 (Yellow) and a bold font.
Add a pulsing #FFFF00 (Yellow) circle animation around the changing bit to represent a digital pulse.

section_3.title: The Hidden Connection: Move = Bit Position
lecture_lines: Position one is disk one; position two is disk two.
Move four uses bit three for the largest disk.
Binary digits guide every move without complex recursion.
animations: Split screen: Left side shows text 'Move 2: 010'. Right side shows 3 disks on pegs.
In the binary string '010', the second bit (position 2) glows #FF8C00 (Orange).
On the right, Disk 2 (the medium one) glows #FF8C00 (Orange) and lifts slightly to show it is the one to move.

section_4.title: The Directional Logic: Odd vs. Even
lecture_lines: Smallest disk always follows a clockwise circular path.
For larger disks, only one legal move is possible.
Binary tells you when, rules tell you where.
animations: Show Disk 1 (Red) moving in a cyclic path: Peg A -> Peg B -> Peg C -> Peg A with a #ADD8E6 (Light Blue) motion trail.
Display Disk 2 (Green) and highlight the only peg it can move to without violating Rule 2 with a #00FF00 (Green) arrow.
Animate a 'Slow' icon vs a 'Fast' icon next to Disk 2 and Disk 1 respectively to emphasize their different roles.

section_5.title: The 3-Disk Synchronized Walkthrough
lecture_lines: Move one: Bit one flips, move the smallest disk.
Move two: Bit two flips, move the medium disk.
Move three: Bit one flips, move the smallest disk.
Move four: Bit three flips, move the largest disk.
Follow the binary pulse until the tower is complete.
animations: Rapidly sequence moves 1-3 (1->B, 2->C, 1->C) while a binary counter (001, 010, 011) updates in #00FFFF (Cyan).
Move 4: Disk 3 moves from A to B. The binary '100' glows #FF00FF (Magenta) and scales up 1.5x.
Execute moves 5-7 (1->A, 2->B, 1->B) sequentially to complete the tower.
Display the equation '2^3 - 1 = 7' in centered #FFFFFF text and pulse it twice.
The completed tower on Peg B flashes with a #FFD700 (Gold) outline to celebrate the solution.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Mathematical Elegance
lecture_lines: Abstract binary numbers perfectly map to this physical puzzle.
Solution takes exactly two to the n minus one moves.
Mathematics reveals hidden order in legendary complexity.
animations: Show a digital counter iterating rapidly from 1 to 2^n-1 in #00FFFF (Cyan) to show scalability.
Display the general formula 'Moves = 2^n - 1' in large, centered #00FF00 (Green) text.
Fade out all elements into a starry background while a silhouette of Professor Hoot appears in the center.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Legend and the Rules", [
            "Welcome to the legendary Towers of Hanoi puzzle.",
            "We have three pegs and stacked disks.",
            "Move one disk; never place larger on smaller."
        ])

        # Define colors
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show three pegs (labeled A, B, C) and 3 disks (Red, Green, Blue) on Peg A.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        peg_a = Rectangle(height=2.5, width=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_b = Rectangle(height=2.5, width=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_c = Rectangle(height=2.5, width=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "D6")
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=20, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "F6")
        
        disk_blue = RoundedRectangle(width=1.4, height=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        disk_green = RoundedRectangle(width=1.0, height=0.3, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        disk_red = RoundedRectangle(width=0.6, height=0.3, color=RED, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        
        # Stacking on Peg A (D2)
        disk_blue.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.8)
        disk_green.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.4)
        disk_red.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + UP * 0.0)
        
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c)
        labels = VGroup(label_a, label_b, label_c)
        disks = VGroup(disk_blue, disk_green, disk_red)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pegs), FadeIn(labels), FadeIn(disks))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the three pegs with #FFD700 (Gold) glow.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        glows = VGroup(*[
            peg.copy().set_stroke(COLOR_GOLD, 10).set_fill(opacity=0)
            for peg in pegs
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(glows))
        self.play(FadeOut(glows))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Move smallest disk (Red) A -> B. Then Green A -> B (fail). Goal on C.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # 1. Red disk moves A -> B
        target_b_top = self.grid["D4"] + DOWN * 0.8
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(target_b_top))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 2. Green disk moves A -> B (attempt)
        illegal_pos = target_b_top + UP * 0.4
        self.play(disk_green.animate.move_to(illegal_pos))
        
        # 3. Show red 'X'
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT, color=COLOR_RED),
            Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT, color=COLOR_RED)
        ).scale(0.3).move_to(illegal_pos + UP * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.play(Flash(cross, color=COLOR_RED))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 4. Return Green and Red to A for "reset" look or just proceed to goal
        self.play(FadeOut(cross), disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.4))
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + UP * 0.0))
        
        # 5. Flash goal stack on Peg C
        # Move all to C
        stack_c = VGroup(disk_blue, disk_green, disk_red)
        self.play(
            disk_blue.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.8),
            disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.4),
            disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + UP * 0.0)
        )
        
        self.play(
            stack_c.animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN),
            Flash(self.grid["D6"], color=COLOR_GREEN, flash_radius=1.5)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"• {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift x to the right side (1.0 to 6.0)
                # Shift y from top to bottom (2.0 to -3.0)
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture lines from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "Smallest disk always follows a clockwise circular path.",
            "For larger disks, only one legal move is possible.",
            "Binary tells you when, rules tell you where."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("The Directional Logic: Odd vs. Even", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        DISK1_COLOR = RED
        DISK2_COLOR = GREEN
        TRAIL_COLOR = "#ADD8E6"
        ARROW_COLOR = "#00FF00"

        # Pegs (Base for visual context)
        peg_a_base = Line(self.grid["D2"] + LEFT*0.4, self.grid["D2"] + RIGHT*0.4, color=GRAY)
        peg_b_base = Line(self.grid["D4"] + LEFT*0.4, self.grid["D4"] + RIGHT*0.4, color=GRAY)
        peg_c_base = Line(self.grid["D6"] + LEFT*0.4, self.grid["D6"] + RIGHT*0.4, color=GRAY)
        peg_a_stem = Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["B2"], color=GRAY)
        peg_b_stem = Line(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["B4"], color=GRAY)
        peg_c_stem = Line(self.grid["D6"], self.grid["B6"], color=GRAY)
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a_base, peg_b_base, peg_c_base, peg_a_stem, peg_b_stem, peg_c_stem)
        self.add(pegs)

        # Labels for Pegs
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20).next_to(peg_a_base, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20).next_to(peg_b_base, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=20).next_to(peg_c_base, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.add(label_a, label_b, label_c)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(DISK1_COLOR))

        # Disk 1 (Red)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.2, width=0.6, fill_opacity=1, color=DISK1_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "C2")
        
        # Trail
        trail = TracedPath(disk1.get_center, stroke_color=TRAIL_COLOR, stroke_width=4, dissipating_time=0.5)
        self.add(trail)
        self.add(disk1)

        # Cyclic path: A -> B -> C -> A
        path_points = ["C4", "C6", "C2"]
        for pos in path_points:
            self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid[pos]), run_time=1, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(DISK2_COLOR))

        # Disk 2 (Green)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.2, width=1.0, fill_opacity=1, color=DISK2_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "C2")
        
        # Move Disk 1 to B (it moved to A in the last cycle, so now move to B)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]), run_time=0.5)

        # Highlight legal move for Disk 2: A to C (B is occupied by smaller Disk 1)
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["C6"], color=ARROW_COLOR, buff=0.3)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"]), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow))

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # 'Fast' icon label for Disk 1
        fast_label = Text("Fast", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)

        ])

        # Define colors
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        labels = VGroup(label_a, label_b, label_c)

            for peg in pegs
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(glows))
        self.play(FadeOut(glows))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Move smallest disk (Red) A -> B. Then Green A -> B (fail). Goal on C.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # 1. Red disk moves A -> B
        target_b_top = self.grid["D4"] + DOWN * 0.8
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(target_b_top))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 2. Green disk moves A -> B (attempt)
        illegal_pos = target_b_top + UP * 0.4
        self.play(disk_green.animate.move_to(illegal_pos))

        cross = VGroup(
            Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT, color=COLOR_RED),
            Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT, color=COLOR_RED)
        ).scale(0.3).move_to(illegal_pos + UP * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.play(Flash(cross, color=COLOR_RED))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 4. Return Green and Red to A for "reset" look or just proceed to goal
        self.play(FadeOut(cross), disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.4))
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + UP * 0.0))
        
        # 5. Flash goal stack on Peg C
        # Move all to C
        stack_c = VGroup(disk_blue, disk_green, disk_red)
        self.play(
            disk_blue.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.8),
            disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.4),
            disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + UP * 0.0)
        )
        
        self.play(
            stack_c.animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN),
            Flash(self.grid["D6"], color=COLOR_GREEN, flash_radius=1.5)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse", [
            "Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.",
            "Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.",
            "The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Binary strings 001 to 111
        binary_strings = ["001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"]
        binary_mobjects = []
        binary_vgroup = VGroup()
        
        for s in binary_strings:
            # Create bit-by-bit group to allow individual highlighting
            bits = VGroup(*[Text(bit, font="Monospace", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF") for bit in s])
            bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            binary_mobjects.append(bits)
            binary_vgroup.add(bits)
            
        binary_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        # Position the vertical list on the right side area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A3", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Fade in the binary list one by one
        for bits in binary_mobjects:
            self.play(FadeIn(bits), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation logic for the rightmost bit that is '1'
        # Sequence of indices for rightmost 1 in each binary string:
        # 001(2), 010(1), 011(2), 100(0), 101(2), 110(1), 111(2)
        indices = [2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        
        # Create a persistent pulse circle that we move and flash
        pulse_circle = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=3)
        
        for i, bits in enumerate(binary_mobjects):
            target_idx = indices[i]
            target_bit = bits[target_idx]
            
            # Position pulse circle
            pulse_circle.move_to(target_bit.get_center())
            
            # Highlight and Pulse
            self.play(
                target_bit.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.2),
                FadeIn(pulse_circle),
                pulse_circle.animate.scale(1.3).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                Flash(target_bit, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3, line_length=0.15),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            # Reset pulse circle for next bit
            pulse_circle.scale(1/1.3).set_stroke(opacity=1)
            self.remove(pulse_circle)
            
            # Brief pause between highlights
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(3)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(bits),
            FadeIn(new_bits),
            new_bits.animate.scale(1.5),
            move_disk_anim(2, 0, 1, duration=1.0)
        )
        bits = new_bits

        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # Binary strings 001 to 111
        binary_strings = ["001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"]
        binary_mobjects = []
        binary_vgroup = VGroup()
        
        for s in binary_strings:
            # Create bit-by-bit group to allow individual highlighting
            bits = VGroup(*[Text(bit, font="Monospace", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF") for bit in s])
            bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            binary_mobjects.append(bits)
            binary_vgroup.add(bits)
            
        binary_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        # Position the vertical list on the right side area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A3", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Sequence of indices for rightmost 1 in each binary string:
        # 001(2), 010(1), 011(2), 100(0), 101(2), 110(1), 111(2)
        indices = [2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        
        # Create a persistent pulse circle that we move and flash
        pulse_circle = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=3)
        
        for i, bits in enumerate(binary_mobjects):
            target_idx = indices[i]
            target_bit = bits[target_idx]
            
            # Position pulse circle
            pulse_circle.move_to(target_bit.get_center())
            
            # Highlight and Pulse
            self.play(

                FadeIn(pulse_circle),

                Flash(target_bit, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3, line_length=0.15),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            # Reset pulse circle for next bit
            pulse_circle.scale(1/1.3).set_stroke(opacity=1)
            self.remove(pulse_circle)
            
            # Brief pause between highlights
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(3)

section_1.content: Introduce the Towers of Hanoi puzzle: three pegs and a stack of disks in decreasing size. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Set the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
section_1.example: An owl professor named 'Hoot' presents three golden pegs and three disks (Red, Green, Blue) and asks the viewer to find the shortest path to move them.

Highlight the 'Rightmost Bit Change': every time we increment a number, observe which bit position is the first one to change from the right. This 'pulse' of flipping bits is the heartbeat of the puzzle.
section_2.example: A digital scoreboard showing 001 (1), 010 (2), 011 (3), 100 (4), 101 (5), 110 (6), 111 (7). As the numbers change, the specific 'active' bit glows brightly.

section_3.title: The Hidden Connection: Move = Bit Position
section_3.content: Reveal the core mapping: The move number (in binary) tells you exactly which disk to move. If the rightmost '1' is in the 1st position, move Disk 1 (the smallest). If it's in the 2nd position, move Disk 2, and so on. This eliminates the need for complex recursion in the player's head.
section_3.example: A split-screen: On the left, binary 010 (Move 2) has its '1' in the second slot. On the right, Disk 2 (the medium one) automatically highlights, signaling it is its turn to move.

section_4.title: The Directional Logic: Odd vs. Even
section_4.content: Explain where to move the disks. For the smallest disk (Disk 1), follow a consistent cyclic path (e.g., Peg A -> Peg B -> Peg C -> Peg A). For other disks, there is always only one legal move possible that doesn't violate the 'large-on-small' rule.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Mathematical Elegance

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse", [
            "Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.",
            "Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.",
            "The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Binary strings 001 to 111
        binary_strings = ["001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"]
        binary_mobjects = []
        binary_vgroup = VGroup()
        
        for s in binary_strings:
            # Create bit-by-bit group to allow individual highlighting
            bits = VGroup(*[Text(bit, font="Monospace", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF") for bit in s])
            bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            binary_mobjects.append(bits)
            binary_vgroup.add(bits)
            
        binary_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        # Position the vertical list on the right side area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A3", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Fade in the binary list one by one
        for bits in binary_mobjects:
            self.play(FadeIn(bits), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation logic for the rightmost bit that is '1'
        # Sequence of indices for rightmost 1 in each binary string:
        # 001(2), 010(1), 011(2), 100(0), 101(2), 110(1), 111(2)
        indices = [2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        
        # Create a persistent pulse circle that we move and flash
        pulse_circle = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=3)
        
        for i, bits in enumerate(binary_mobjects):
            target_idx = indices[i]
            target_bit = bits[target_idx]
            
            # Position pulse circle
            pulse_circle.move_to(target_bit.get_center())
            
            # Highlight and Pulse
            self.play(
                target_bit.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.2),
                FadeIn(pulse_circle),
                pulse_circle.animate.scale(1.3).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                Flash(target_bit, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3, line_length=0.15),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            # Reset pulse circle for next bit
            pulse_circle.scale(1/1.3).set_stroke(opacity=1)
            self.remove(pulse_circle)
            
            # Brief pause between highlights
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(3)

            peg_stacks[from_peg].remove(disk)
            target_h = len(peg_stacks[to_peg])
            target_pos = get_peg_bottom(to_peg) + UP * (0.2 + target_h * 0.41)
            peg_stacks[to_peg].append(disk)
            return disk.animate(run_time=duration, path_arc=PI/2).move_to(target_pos)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("001", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("010", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(1, 0, 2, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("011", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(0, 1, 2, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(MAGENTA))
        new_bits = update_bits("100", bits).set_color(MAGENTA)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(bits),
            FadeIn(new_bits),
            new_bits.animate.scale(1.5),
            move_disk_anim(2, 0, 1, duration=1.0)
        )
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE_C))
        
        # Move 5 (101)
        new_bits_5 = update_bits("101", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_5), move_disk_anim(0, 2, 0, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_5
        
        # Move 6 (110)
        new_bits_6 = update_bits("110", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_6), move_disk_anim(1, 2, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_6
        
        # Move 7 (111)
        new_bits_7 = update_bits("111", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_7), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_7
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Equation: 2^3 - 1 = 7 pulse
        equation = MathTex("2^3 - 1 = 7", color=WHITE_C, font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "B4")
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), Write(equation))
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(equation.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(equation.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.3)
        
        # Completion Flash: Gold outline on tower on Peg B
        tower = VGroup(disk3, disk2, disk1)
        glow = tower.copy().set_style(stroke_color=GOLD, stroke_width=6, fill_opacity=0)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(Flash(tower, color=GOLD, flash_radius=1.5))
        self.play(FadeOut(glow))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np
import random

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Conclusion: Mathematical Elegance", 
            [
                "Abstract binary numbers perfectly map to this physical puzzle.",
                "Solution takes exactly two to the n minus one moves.",
                "Mathematics reveals hidden order in legendary complexity."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color: #00FFFF (Cyan)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Show a digital counter iterating rapidly from 1 to 2^n-1 in #00FFFF (Cyan)
        # Using ValueTracker for efficient numerical updates
        counter_val = ValueTracker(1)
        counter_num = DecimalNumber(
            1, 
            num_decimal_places=0, 
            group_with_commas=True, 
            font_size=40,
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        self.place_in_area(counter_num, "C1", "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # updater to change value in place
        counter_num.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(counter_val.get_value()))
        
        self.add(counter_num)
        # Iterate to a large number representing 2^n-1 scalability
        self.play(counter_val.animate.set_value(10**14), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(counter_num))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color: #00FF00 (Green)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Display the general formula 'Moves = 2^n - 1' in large, centered #00FF00 (Green) text.
        formula = MathTex("Moves = 2^n - 1", color="#00FF00", font_size=60)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color: #FFFFFF (White)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Fade out all elements into a starry background while a silhouette of Professor Hoot appears in the center.
        
        # Create stars
        stars = VGroup(*[
            Dot(
                point=[random.uniform(0.1, 6.5), random.uniform(-3.5, 3.5), 0],
                radius=random.uniform(0.01, 0.04),
                color=WHITE,
                fill_opacity=random.uniform(0.2, 0.7)
            ) for _ in range(100)
        ])
        
        # Procedural silhouette of Professor Hoot (Owl shape)
        body = Ellipse(width=1.2, height=1.6, color="#111111", fill_opacity=1)
        head = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#111111", fill_opacity=1).next_to(body, UP, buff=-0.2)
        ear_l = Triangle(color="#111111", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15).rotate(30*DEGREES).move_to(head.get_top() + LEFT*0.25)
        ear_r = Triangle(color="#111111", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15).rotate(-30*DEGREES).move_to(head.get_top() + RIGHT*0.25)
        hoot = VGroup(body, head, ear_l, ear_r)
        self.place_in_area(hoot, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=1.5)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(self.title),
            FadeOut(self.lecture),
            FadeIn(stars),
            FadeIn(hoot),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
outline.content: Introduce binary counting from 0 to 7 (for a 3-disk puzzle). Visualize the bits flipping. Highlight the 'Rightmost Bit Change': every time we increment a number, observe which bit position is the first one to change from the right. This 'pulse' of flipping bits is the heartbeat of the puzzle.
outline.example: A digital scoreboard showing 001 (1), 010 (2), 011 (3), 100 (4), 101 (5), 110 (6), 111 (7). As the numbers change, the specific 'active' bit glows brightly.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
lecture_lines: Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
animations: Display a vertical list of binary numbers 001 to 111 in #00FFFF (Cyan) on the left side.
As the counter increments, highlight the rightmost bit that flips using #FFFF00 (Yellow) and a bold font.
Add a pulsing #FFFF00 (Yellow) circle animation around the changing bit to represent a digital pulse.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse", [
            "Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.",
            "Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.",
            "The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Binary strings 001 to 111
        binary_strings = ["001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"]
        binary_mobjects = []
        binary_vgroup = VGroup()
        
        for s in binary_strings:
            # Create bit-by-bit group to allow individual highlighting
            bits = VGroup(*[Text(bit, font="Monospace", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF") for bit in s])
            bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            binary_mobjects.append(bits)
            binary_vgroup.add(bits)
            
        binary_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        # Position the vertical list on the right side area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A3", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Fade in the binary list one by one
        for bits in binary_mobjects:
            self.play(FadeIn(bits), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation logic for the rightmost bit that is '1'
        # Sequence of indices for rightmost 1 in each binary string:
        # 001(2), 010(1), 011(2), 100(0), 101(2), 110(1), 111(2)
        indices = [2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        
        # Create a persistent pulse circle that we move and flash
        pulse_circle = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=3)
        
        for i, bits in enumerate(binary_mobjects):
            target_idx = indices[i]
            target_bit = bits[target_idx]
            
            # Position pulse circle
            pulse_circle.move_to(target_bit.get_center())
            
            # Highlight and Pulse
            self.play(
                target_bit.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.2),
                FadeIn(pulse_circle),
                pulse_circle.animate.scale(1.3).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                Flash(target_bit, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3, line_length=0.15),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            # Reset pulse circle for next bit
            pulse_circle.scale(1/1.3).set_stroke(opacity=1)
            self.remove(pulse_circle)
            
            # Brief pause between highlights
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Legend and the Rules
outline.content: Introduce the Towers of Hanoi puzzle: three pegs and a stack of disks in decreasing size. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Set the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
outline.example: An owl professor named 'Hoot' presents three golden pegs and three disks (Red, Green, Blue) and asks the viewer to find the shortest path to move them.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Legend and the Rules", [
            "Welcome to the legendary Towers of Hanoi puzzle.",
            "We have three pegs and stacked disks.",
            "Move one disk; never place larger on smaller."
        ])

        # Define colors
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show three pegs (labeled A, B, C) and 3 disks (Red, Green, Blue) on Peg A.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        peg_a = Rectangle(height=2.5, width=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_b = Rectangle(height=2.5, width=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_c = Rectangle(height=2.5, width=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "D6")
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=20, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "F6")
        
        disk_blue = RoundedRectangle(width=1.4, height=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        disk_green = RoundedRectangle(width=1.0, height=0.3, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        disk_red = RoundedRectangle(width=0.6, height=0.3, color=RED, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        
        # Stacking on Peg A (D2)
        disk_blue.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.8)
        disk_green.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.4)
        disk_red.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + UP * 0.0)
        
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c)
        labels = VGroup(label_a, label_b, label_c)
        disks = VGroup(disk_blue, disk_green, disk_red)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pegs), FadeIn(labels), FadeIn(disks))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the three pegs with #FFD700 (Gold) glow.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        glows = VGroup(*[
            peg.copy().set_stroke(COLOR_GOLD, 10).set_fill(opacity=0)
            for peg in pegs
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(glows))
        self.play(FadeOut(glows))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Move smallest disk (Red) A -> B. Then Green A -> B (fail). Goal on C.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # 1. Red disk moves A -> B
        target_b_top = self.grid["D4"] + DOWN * 0.8
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(target_b_top))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 2. Green disk moves A -> B (attempt)
        illegal_pos = target_b_top + UP * 0.4
        self.play(disk_green.animate.move_to(illegal_pos))
        
        # 3. Show red 'X'
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT, color=COLOR_RED),
            Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT, color=COLOR_RED)
        ).scale(0.3).move_to(illegal_pos + UP * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.play(Flash(cross, color=COLOR_RED))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 4. Return Green and Red to A for "reset" look or just proceed to goal
        self.play(FadeOut(cross), disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.4))
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + UP * 0.0))
        
        # 5. Flash goal stack on Peg C
        # Move all to C
        stack_c = VGroup(disk_blue, disk_green, disk_red)
        self.play(
            disk_blue.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.8),
            disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.4),
            disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + UP * 0.0)
        )
        
        self.play(
            stack_c.animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN),
            Flash(self.grid["D6"], color=COLOR_GREEN, flash_radius=1.5)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

outline.title: The Hidden Connection: Move = Bit Position
outline.content: Reveal the core mapping: The move number (in binary) tells you exactly which disk to move. If the rightmost '1' is in the 1st position, move Disk 1 (the smallest). If it's in the 2nd position, move Disk 2, and so on. This eliminates the need for complex recursion in the player's head.
outline.example: A split-screen: On the left, binary 010 (Move 2) has its '1' in the second slot. On the right, Disk 2 (the medium one) automatically highlights, signaling it is its turn to move.

outline.title: The Directional Logic: Odd vs. Even
outline.content: Explain where to move the disks. For the smallest disk (Disk 1), follow a consistent cyclic path (e.g., Peg A -> Peg B -> Peg C -> Peg A). For other disks, there is always only one legal move possible that doesn't violate the 'large-on-small' rule.
outline.example: Disk 1 is portrayed as a hyperactive rabbit hopping in a circle: Peg 1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 1. The larger disks are 'slow turtles' that only move when the binary counter tells them to, landing on the only available legal spot.

        self.add(self.title)

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        slow_label.next_to(disk2, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Write(fast_label), Write(slow_label))
        
        # Small visual emphasis: Fast disk hops while slow disk stays
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.shift(UP * 0.3).set_rate_func(rate_functions.there_and_back),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.shift(UP * 0.3).set_rate_func(rate_functions.there_and_back),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        self.wait(2)

                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 3-Disk Synchronized Walkthrough", [
            "Move one: Bit one flips, move the smallest disk.",
            "Move two: Bit two flips, move the medium disk.",
            "Move three: Bit one flips, move the smallest disk.",
            "Move four: Bit three flips, move the largest disk.",
            "Follow the binary pulse until the tower is complete."
        ])

        # Colors
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        MAGENTA = "#FF00FF"
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        WHITE_C = "#FFFFFF"
        DISK_COLORS = ["#3377FF", "#33FF77", "#FF7733"] # Blue, Green, Orange-ish

        # Disks and Pegs setup
        peg_a = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color=GRAY_A, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_b = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color=GRAY_A, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_c = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color=GRAY_A, fill_opacity=1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "D6")
        
        pegs = [peg_a, peg_b, peg_c]
        self.add(*pegs)

        # Disks: 0=Smallest, 1=Medium, 2=Largest
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.8, fill_color=DISK_COLORS[0], fill_opacity=1)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.4, fill_color=DISK_COLORS[1], fill_opacity=1)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.0, fill_color=DISK_COLORS[2], fill_opacity=1)
        
        disks = [disk1, disk2, disk3]
        
        # Initial positions
        peg_stacks = [[disk3, disk2, disk1], [], []]
        
        def get_peg_bottom(peg_index):
            return pegs[peg_index].get_bottom()

        for i, disk in enumerate(peg_stacks[0]):
            disk.move_to(get_peg_bottom(0) + UP * (0.2 + i * 0.41))
        
        self.add(disk1, disk2, disk3)

        # Binary Counter
        bits = VGroup(Text("0", font_size=36), Text("0", font_size=36), Text("0", font_size=36)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(bits, "B4")
        self.add(bits)

        def update_bits(val_str, current_bits):
            new_bits = VGroup(Text(val_str[0], font_size=36), Text(val_str[1], font_size=36), Text(val_str[2], font_size=36)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
            new_bits.move_to(current_bits.get_center())
            return new_bits

        def move_disk_anim(disk_idx, from_peg, to_peg, duration=0.8):
            disk = disks[disk_idx]
            peg_stacks[from_peg].remove(disk)
            target_h = len(peg_stacks[to_peg])
            target_pos = get_peg_bottom(to_peg) + UP * (0.2 + target_h * 0.41)
            peg_stacks[to_peg].append(disk)
            return disk.animate(run_time=duration, path_arc=PI/2).move_to(target_pos)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("001", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("010", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(1, 0, 2, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("011", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(0, 1, 2, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(MAGENTA))
        new_bits = update_bits("100", bits).set_color(MAGENTA)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(bits),
            FadeIn(new_bits),
            new_bits.animate.scale(1.5),
            move_disk_anim(2, 0, 1, duration=1.0)
        )
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE_C))
        
        # Move 5 (101)
        new_bits_5 = update_bits("101", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_5), move_disk_anim(0, 2, 0, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_5
        
        # Move 6 (110)
        new_bits_6 = update_bits("110", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_6), move_disk_anim(1, 2, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_6
        
        # Move 7 (111)
        new_bits_7 = update_bits("111", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_7), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_7
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Equation: 2^3 - 1 = 7 pulse
        equation = MathTex("2^3 - 1 = 7", color=WHITE_C, font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "B4")
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), Write(equation))
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(equation.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(equation.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.3)
        
        # Completion Flash: Gold outline on tower on Peg B
        tower = VGroup(disk3, disk2, disk1)
        glow = tower.copy().set_style(stroke_color=GOLD, stroke_width=6, fill_opacity=0)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(Flash(tower, color=GOLD, flash_radius=1.5))
        self.play(FadeOut(glow))
        self.wait(2)

            "Move one disk; never place larger on smaller."
        ])

        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "F4")

        disk_green = RoundedRectangle(width=1.0, height=0.3, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        disk_red = RoundedRectangle(width=0.6, height=0.3, color=RED, fill_opacity=1, corner_radius=0.1)
        
        # Stacking on Peg A (D2)
        disk_blue.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.8)
        disk_green.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.4)
        disk_red.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + UP * 0.0)
        
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c)
        labels = VGroup(label_a, label_b, label_c)
        disks = VGroup(disk_blue, disk_green, disk_red)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        glows = VGroup(*[
            peg.copy().set_stroke(COLOR_GOLD, 10).set_fill(opacity=0)
            for peg in pegs
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(glows))
        self.play(FadeOut(glows))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Move smallest disk (Red) A -> B. Then Green A -> B (fail). Goal on C.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # 1. Red disk moves A -> B
        target_b_top = self.grid["D4"] + DOWN * 0.8
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(target_b_top))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 2. Green disk moves A -> B (attempt)
        illegal_pos = target_b_top + UP * 0.4
        self.play(disk_green.animate.move_to(illegal_pos))
        
        # 3. Show red 'X'
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT, color=COLOR_RED),
            Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT, color=COLOR_RED)
        ).scale(0.3).move_to(illegal_pos + UP * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.play(Flash(cross, color=COLOR_RED))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 4. Return Green and Red to A for "reset" look or just proceed to goal
        self.play(FadeOut(cross), disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.4))
        self.play(disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + UP * 0.0))
        
        # 5. Flash goal stack on Peg C
        # Move all to C
        stack_c = VGroup(disk_blue, disk_green, disk_red)
        self.play(
            disk_blue.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.8),
            disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + DOWN * 0.4),
            disk_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"] + UP * 0.0)
        )
        
        self.play(
            stack_c.animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN),
            Flash(self.grid["D6"], color=COLOR_GREEN, flash_radius=1.5)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse", [
            "Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.",
            "Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.",
            "The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Binary strings 001 to 111
        binary_strings = ["001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"]
        binary_mobjects = []
        binary_vgroup = VGroup()
        
        for s in binary_strings:
            # Create bit-by-bit group to allow individual highlighting
            bits = VGroup(*[Text(bit, font="Monospace", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF") for bit in s])
            bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            binary_mobjects.append(bits)
            binary_vgroup.add(bits)
            
        binary_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        # Position the vertical list on the right side area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A3", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Fade in the binary list one by one
        for bits in binary_mobjects:
            self.play(FadeIn(bits), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation logic for the rightmost bit that is '1'
        # Sequence of indices for rightmost 1 in each binary string:
        # 001(2), 010(1), 011(2), 100(0), 101(2), 110(1), 111(2)
        indices = [2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        
        # Create a persistent pulse circle that we move and flash
        pulse_circle = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=3)
        
        for i, bits in enumerate(binary_mobjects):
            target_idx = indices[i]
            target_bit = bits[target_idx]
            
            # Position pulse circle
            pulse_circle.move_to(target_bit.get_center())
            
            # Highlight and Pulse
            self.play(
                target_bit.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.2),
                FadeIn(pulse_circle),
                pulse_circle.animate.scale(1.3).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                Flash(target_bit, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3, line_length=0.15),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            # Reset pulse circle for next bit
            pulse_circle.scale(1/1.3).set_stroke(opacity=1)
            self.remove(pulse_circle)
            
            # Brief pause between highlights
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(3)

        # Lecture lines from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "Smallest disk always follows a clockwise circular path.",
            "For larger disks, only one legal move is possible.",
            "Binary tells you when, rules tell you where."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("The Directional Logic: Odd vs. Even", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        DISK1_COLOR = RED
        DISK2_COLOR = GREEN
        TRAIL_COLOR = "#ADD8E6"
        ARROW_COLOR = "#00FF00"

        # Pegs (Base for visual context)
        peg_a_base = Line(self.grid["D2"] + LEFT*0.4, self.grid["D2"] + RIGHT*0.4, color=GRAY)
        peg_b_base = Line(self.grid["D4"] + LEFT*0.4, self.grid["D4"] + RIGHT*0.4, color=GRAY)
        peg_c_base = Line(self.grid["D6"] + LEFT*0.4, self.grid["D6"] + RIGHT*0.4, color=GRAY)
        peg_a_stem = Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["B2"], color=GRAY)
        peg_b_stem = Line(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["B4"], color=GRAY)
        peg_c_stem = Line(self.grid["D6"], self.grid["B6"], color=GRAY)
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a_base, peg_b_base, peg_c_base, peg_a_stem, peg_b_stem, peg_c_stem)

        self.add(trail)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 3-Disk Synchronized Walkthrough", [
            "Move one: Bit one flips, move the smallest disk.",
            "Move two: Bit two flips, move the medium disk.",
            "Move three: Bit one flips, move the smallest disk.",
            "Move four: Bit three flips, move the largest disk.",
            "Follow the binary pulse until the tower is complete."
        ])

        # Colors
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        MAGENTA = "#FF00FF"
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        WHITE_C = "#FFFFFF"
        DISK_COLORS = ["#3377FF", "#33FF77", "#FF7733"] # Blue, Green, Orange-ish

        # Disks and Pegs setup
        peg_a = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color=GRAY_A, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_b = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color=GRAY_A, fill_opacity=1)
        peg_c = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color=GRAY_A, fill_opacity=1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "D6")
        
        pegs = [peg_a, peg_b, peg_c]
        self.add(*pegs)

        # Disks: 0=Smallest, 1=Medium, 2=Largest
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.8, fill_color=DISK_COLORS[0], fill_opacity=1)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.4, fill_color=DISK_COLORS[1], fill_opacity=1)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.0, fill_color=DISK_COLORS[2], fill_opacity=1)
        
        disks = [disk1, disk2, disk3]
        
        # Initial positions
        peg_stacks = [[disk3, disk2, disk1], [], []]
        
        def get_peg_bottom(peg_index):
            return pegs[peg_index].get_bottom()

        for i, disk in enumerate(peg_stacks[0]):
            disk.move_to(get_peg_bottom(0) + UP * (0.2 + i * 0.41))
        
        self.add(disk1, disk2, disk3)

        # Binary Counter
        bits = VGroup(Text("0", font_size=36), Text("0", font_size=36), Text("0", font_size=36)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(bits, "B4")
        self.add(bits)

        def update_bits(val_str, current_bits):
            new_bits = VGroup(Text(val_str[0], font_size=36), Text(val_str[1], font_size=36), Text(val_str[2], font_size=36)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
            new_bits.move_to(current_bits.get_center())
            return new_bits

        def move_disk_anim(disk_idx, from_peg, to_peg, duration=0.8):
            disk = disks[disk_idx]
            peg_stacks[from_peg].remove(disk)
            target_h = len(peg_stacks[to_peg])
            target_pos = get_peg_bottom(to_peg) + UP * (0.2 + target_h * 0.41)
            peg_stacks[to_peg].append(disk)
            return disk.animate(run_time=duration, path_arc=PI/2).move_to(target_pos)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("001", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("010", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(1, 0, 2, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        new_bits = update_bits("011", bits).set_color(CYAN)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits), move_disk_anim(0, 1, 2, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(MAGENTA))
        new_bits = update_bits("100", bits).set_color(MAGENTA)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(bits),
            FadeIn(new_bits),
            new_bits.animate.scale(1.5),
            move_disk_anim(2, 0, 1, duration=1.0)
        )
        bits = new_bits

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE_C))
        
        # Move 5 (101)
        new_bits_5 = update_bits("101", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_5), move_disk_anim(0, 2, 0, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_5
        
        # Move 6 (110)
        new_bits_6 = update_bits("110", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_6), move_disk_anim(1, 2, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_6
        
        # Move 7 (111)
        new_bits_7 = update_bits("111", bits).scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), FadeIn(new_bits_7), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 1, duration=0.6))
        bits = new_bits_7
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Equation: 2^3 - 1 = 7 pulse
        equation = MathTex("2^3 - 1 = 7", color=WHITE_C, font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "B4")
        self.play(FadeOut(bits), Write(equation))
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(equation.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(equation.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.3)
        
        # Completion Flash: Gold outline on tower on Peg B
        tower = VGroup(disk3, disk2, disk1)
        glow = tower.copy().set_style(stroke_color=GOLD, stroke_width=6, fill_opacity=0)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(Flash(tower, color=GOLD, flash_radius=1.5))

        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse", [
            "Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.",
            "Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.",
            "The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Binary strings 001 to 111
        binary_strings = ["001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"]
        binary_mobjects = []
        binary_vgroup = VGroup()
        
        for s in binary_strings:
            # Create bit-by-bit group to allow individual highlighting
            # Use Monospace for aligned columns
            bits = VGroup(*[Text(bit, font="Monospace", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF") for bit in s])
            bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            binary_mobjects.append(bits)
            binary_vgroup.add(bits)
            
        binary_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        # [RESOLVE ISSUE 29] Position the vertical list on the right side area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, 'A4', 'F4', scale_factor=1.1)
        
        # Fade in the binary list one by one
        for bits in binary_mobjects:
            self.play(FadeIn(bits), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation logic for the rightmost bit that is '1'
        # Sequence of indices for rightmost 1 in each binary string:
        # 001(2), 010(1), 011(2), 100(0), 101(2), 110(1), 111(2)
        indices = [2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        
        # Pulse indicator (not added to scene yet)
        pulse_circle = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=3)
        
        for i, bits in enumerate(binary_mobjects):
            target_idx = indices[i]
            target_bit = bits[target_idx]
            
            # Highlight and Pulse
            # We use a copy of pulse_circle for the animation
            temp_pulse = pulse_circle.copy().move_to(target_bit.get_center())
            self.add(temp_pulse)
            
            self.play(
                target_bit.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
                temp_pulse.animate.scale(2.5).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                Flash(target_bit, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.25, line_length=0.1, num_lines=8),
                run_time=0.6
            )
            self.remove(temp_pulse)
            
            # Brief pause between highlights

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse", [
            "Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.",
            "Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.",
            "The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Solve this puzzle using the heartbeat of binary counting.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Watch bits flip as we count zero to seven.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Binary strings 001 to 111
        binary_strings = ["001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"]
        binary_mobjects = []
        binary_vgroup = VGroup()
        
        for s in binary_strings:
            # Create bit-by-bit group to allow individual highlighting
            # Use Monospace for aligned columns
            bits = VGroup(*[Text(bit, font="Monospace", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF") for bit in s])
            bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            binary_mobjects.append(bits)
            binary_vgroup.add(bits)
            
        binary_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        # [RESOLVE ISSUE 29] Position the vertical list on the right side area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, 'A4', 'F4', scale_factor=1.1)
        
        # Fade in the binary list one by one
        for bits in binary_mobjects:
            self.play(FadeIn(bits), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The rightmost changing bit tells which disk to move.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation logic for the rightmost bit that is '1'
        # Sequence of indices for rightmost 1 in each binary string:
        # 001(2), 010(1), 011(2), 100(0), 101(2), 110(1), 111(2)
        indices = [2, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
        
        # Pulse indicator (not added to scene yet)
        pulse_circle = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=3)
        
        for i, bits in enumerate(binary_mobjects):
            target_idx = indices[i]
            target_bit = bits[target_idx]
            
            # Highlight and Pulse
            # We use a copy of pulse_circle for the animation
            temp_pulse = pulse_circle.copy().move_to(target_bit.get_center())
            self.add(temp_pulse)
            
            self.play(
                target_bit.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
                temp_pulse.animate.scale(2.5).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                Flash(target_bit, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.25, line_length=0.1, num_lines=8),
                run_time=0.6
            )
            self.remove(temp_pulse)
            
            # Brief pause between highlights
            self.wait(0.1)

        self.wait(2)

        # 2. Green disk moves A -> B (attempt)
        illegal_pos = [self.grid["C4"][0], base_y + 0.35, 0] # Above Red on B
        self.play(disk_green.animate.move_to(illegal_pos))
        
        # 3. Show red 'X'
